title: Phage display with machine learning finds peptide binders in KRAS-defined lung cancer
summary: Phage display on lung cancer cell lines with KRAS wild-type, G12C, G12D and G12V backgrounds produced sequencing data used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From its candidates, 98 non-redundant heptapeptides were selected for synthesis, and 88 were solubilized and tested by flow cytometry. Binding was heterogeneous, with broad pan-cellular binders and candidates showing mutant-versus-wild-type preference; dose-response and normal-cell counter-screens prioritized candidates. Hit-rate numbers are not given in the abstract and the work is limited to cell lines.
ai_technology: Multimodal probabilistic model trained on phage-display sequencing outputs to generate peptide candidates
organization: INSERM; Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives; Institut de Recherche Interdisciplinaire de Grenoble

evidence.tested: Flow cytometry, dose-response profiling and normal-cell counter-screening of 88 synthesized peptides.
evidence.unknown: Hit rates, in vivo targeting and clinical relevance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A probabilistic model trained on selection data generated the candidate peptides.
